extracted.intended_audience: publishers, librarians, journal editors, researchers, and scholarly-communication stakeholders
extracted.subtask_description: Announcement and description of the ANSI/NISO Z39.106-2023 Peer Review Terminology standard intended to standardize language about peer review for journal articles to improve transparency, comparability, and adoption across publications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Simplified terminology to support open research
rubrics_metrics.description: ANSI/NISO Z39.106-2023 'offers a simplified terminology that will make the peer review process more transparent to authors, reviewers, and readers across the journals that adopt it.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The standard's simplified terminology is intended to clarify communication about peer review roles and practices, aiding transparency for all stakeholders; it is presented as a foundational feature to support open research.

rubrics_metrics.name: Standardize peer review roles and practices
rubrics_metrics.description: The standard 'will support open research by simplifying the communication of peer review roles and practices and fostering greater transparency in the peer review process.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Standardized definitions of roles and practices reduce variance in nomenclature across publications and make processes easier to understand and report; the standard builds on STM working group definitions and NISO development.

rubrics_metrics.name: Enable comparison of peer review processes across publications
rubrics_metrics.description: A 'shared set of definitions will also enable the community to compare peer review processes across publications more easily.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: By using the same terms and definitions, journals and stakeholders can more readily assess and compare the types of peer review used, facilitating benchmarking and informed choices by authors/readers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope: developed for articles and journal publications
rubrics_metrics.description: The new standard 'was developed for articles and journal publications,' with possible future extension to books and other peer-reviewed research content.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Current applicability is limited to article- and journal-based workflows; implementers should note this scope and track future NISO Standing Committee work for other content types.

rubrics_metrics.name: Respond to fairness and transparency concerns
rubrics_metrics.description: The standard responds to concerns that 'with the move toward open research and the emergence of new peer review models, concerns around fairness in the peer review process have given rise to demands for greater transparency.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Emphasizes transparency as a remedy to fairness concerns; adopting the terminology is presented as one element of broader efforts to make peer review fairer and more accountable.

rubrics_metrics.name: ANSI/NISO accredited standard status
rubrics_metrics.description: The terminology is published as 'ANSI/NISO Z39.106-2023, Peer Review Terminology.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Being an ANSI/NISO standard signals formal recognition and can encourage wider adoption and trust; implementers may reference the standard identifier when updating policies and systems.

rubrics_metrics.name: Facilitate easy adoption and promulgation
rubrics_metrics.description: As noted by the working group chair: standardization should enable 'easy adoption and promulgation.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The standard was informed by pre-publication trials at publishers and working-group input to make it practical; implementers are encouraged to leverage these precedents and the working-group outputs to streamline uptake.

rubrics_metrics.name: Support implementations through cooperation and open dialogue
rubrics_metrics.description: NISO states its role is 'strengthening overall trust in scholarly communication—in this case, the peer review process—through cooperation and open dialogue' and expresses intent to 'support implementations of this new standard.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adoption is positioned as a community activity; publishers, libraries, and other stakeholders should collaborate with NISO and peers when implementing the terminology to ensure consistent interpretation and use.
